column2: Does every diagram have a “Chart” menu in “From the app”?
column3: Yes. In a diagram’s editor, “From the app” tab, each type starts with “Chart”: ready-made starting points. For columns, bars, pies…: “🧮 Count in my database” and the app’s statistics. For the types that have their own panel (maps, timelines, fan, calendar, survival, occupations, marriages, DNA, child mortality, widowhood…): for example “Birth regions of my ancestors (6 generations)”, “Departures (born here, died elsewhere)”, “Who was alive in 1789”, “My ancestors, by century”; the choice sets the fields of the panel (and the group of people or the period), then click the panel’s “Use…” button. “✏️ Custom” leaves everything to you. The scatter plot, the flow (Sankey), the organisation chart, the two timelines, the figure cards and the target bar also take their data from your database (age at marriage and at death, father’s → son’s occupation, department of birth → of death, your ancestors as an organisation chart, the life of the starting person, the quality of your database…).

column2: How do I note that a person signed a record (or “cannot sign”)?
column3: In “Edit an event”: under the witnesses, “✍️ The person (or the husband) signed” and, for a marriage, “✍️ The wife signed”: Not known, Yes, or No (cannot sign). Each witness also has their own “✍️ Signed the record” box. The “✍️ Able to sign” diagram shows, period by period, the share of husbands, wives and witnesses who could sign.

column2: How do I make a diagram of the woodcutters who had 3 children born in Pernay (combined criteria)?
column3: In a diagram’s editor, “From the app” tab, “Chart” → “✏️ Custom”. Under “Only the people…”, “＋ Criterion” adds as many criteria as you want, the same as in My lists: occupation, number of children (“3 and 3” = exactly 3, “3” then an empty box = at least 3), place of birth, place of death, period of birth or death, sex, living or not, age at death, Sosa generation, label, without a source… “not” reverses a criterion. With two or more criteria, choose “all these criteria (AND)” or “at least one (OR)”. Then “What is counted” and “Group by” (decade of birth, commune, occupation, age at marriage, age at first child, number of unions, branch, with or without a source…). The sentence above the preview reads the setting back and says how many people are found (“People, occupation “woodcutter”, having 3 children, born in “Pernay”, by decade — 2 people found”). A click on a bar or a slice opens the list of these people. The ready-made starting points are arranged by section (People, Couples, Children, Places, Occupations, Dates, My research, Media); those that make no sense for the chosen drawing are greyed out “not for this diagram” (for example decades in a pie chart).

column2: How do I create my own chart from external data (Wikipedia, spreadsheet, image)?
column3: Wherever you place a diagram, “⤒ Import”: 📄 File (CSV, or an LCNDA diagram or chart), 📋 Paste a table (first column = the names, following columns = the figures, a row of headings becomes the names of the series), 🌐 Wikipedia page (paste the address: the tables and chart images of the page appear, choose one; you need the Internet), 🖼️ Image of a chart (pie, bars, columns, line or hemicycle: the app spots the colours and suggests the slices, lengths or seats; you name them, correct them, give the real top value). Then you choose the drawing and set everything in the editor. The step-by-step guide is also in the ⚙️ of the diagram gallery.

column2: How do I say that a person was an athlete, an elected official, a soldier, a farmer… (profiles)?
column3: On their record, the “🧩 This person was…” block → “🧩 Choose their profiles…” (or Edit the record → “Blocks to show” → “🧩 Profiles…”). Tick one or more profiles (Artist, Athlete, Politician, Local elected official, Soldier, Farmer, Teacher…), then “Apply”. Each profile adds its sections to the person’s page. A person can have several; unticking a profile hides its sections without erasing what you wrote in them. The “Artist” box on the record and the “Artist” profile are the same thing.

column2: How do I create my own profile (brass band musician, beekeeper…)?
column3: In the profiles window: “＋ Create my own profile…”. In 3 steps: 1 · the name, the icon and the colour; 2 · the sections, taken from other profiles (the artist’s concerts, the athlete’s statistics…) or your own (a table, linked records, images, a text); 3 · the order of the page. Your profile goes into “✎ My profiles” and is ticked like the others.

column2: How do I see the page of a person who has several profiles (artist, athlete, mayor…)?
column3: “🧩 This person was…” block → “Open their page”. At the top: “All together” (a single page with the sections of all their profiles, and the life timeline coloured by profile) or one profile at a time. “⚙️ Organise the page”: arrange the profiles and sections (⠿ or ↑ ↓), hide some (👁), choose the width (full line, ½, ⅓), “Setting specific to this person”, “Hide empty sections”. The coloured edge says which profile a section comes from.

column2: How do I record a politician’s career (terms of office, elections, votes)?
column3: Tick the “🗳 Politician” profile (or “🏛 Local elected official”), then open their page: 🏛 Terms and positions (level, place, dates, predecessor, successor), 🗳 Elections (ballot, round, registered voters, votes, %, result, opponents, poster, election manifesto, results by commune), 👥 Parties, groups and committees, 📜 Texts, votes and proposals, 🏢 Government, 🗣 Speeches, ⚠️ Controversies, 🗺 Map of terms, and the career timeline. “⚙️ Organise” offers templates: Local elected official, Member of parliament, Minister, Activist, Diplomat, Senior civil servant.

column2: How do I record an athlete’s career (clubs, medals, records, statistics)?
column3: Tick the “🏅 Athlete · sportsperson” profile, choose their sport or sports (more than 120, each with its own fields: position and shirt for rugby or football, time and wind for athletics, horse for riding, grades for judo, Elo for chess…). Their page: 🏟 Clubs and teams, 🥇 Medals and titles, ⏱ Records, 📊 Statistics by season (columns depending on the sport, “＋ Add a column”, “🧮 Calculated column”), 🏁 Results (wins, losses, by competition), coaches, injuries and career change, and the timeline of clubs and selections.

column2: How do I keep an artist’s bibliography, works, discography or filmography?
column3: On their record, tick “Artist” (Edit → Blocks to show) and choose their discipline. The blocks 📚 Bibliography, 🖼️ Works and inventory, 💿 Discography (musician, singer, composer, conductor, band) and 🎬 Filmography (filmmaker, actor, videographer) then appear; a block already filled in always stays visible. “See all, edit” opens the catalogue full screen: 🎨 the artist’s page, then one tab per kind (Books, Works, Records, Tracks, Films, Exhibitions; “＋” for the others). Each list has the same bar (🔍 Search, Filter ▾, List | Cards, Sort: by year, by title, catalogue number, value or “My order” with ⠿ ↑ ↓); ＋ New, ⤒ Import, ⤓ Export (PDF, printing, CSV spreadsheet, 💾 re-importable file). If the record is not ticked “Artist” yet, the app offers to tick it when you first save.

column2: How do I make an inventory of an artist’s works?
column3: Artist’s catalogue → 🖼️ Works and inventory: inventory number (suggested after the last one), catalogue raisonné number, technique, support, dimensions, signature, where the work is (in the family, museum, private collection, sold, lent, lost…), exact place, owner, condition, estimated value, provenance, exhibitions, photos. The “Inventory” view gives the table with the total of the values; “🖨 Print the illustrated inventory” puts it on paper with the photos. ⤒ Import: a table from your spreadsheet pasted as it is (columns No., Title, Date, Technique, Dimensions, Place, Owner, Condition, Value… recognised automatically), or the known works from Wikidata (those in museums, with their image).

column2: How do I make a complete discography, track by track, as on Discogs?
column3: Artist’s catalogue → 💿 Discography: each record has its type (album, EP, single, compilation, live, soundtrack…), label, catalogue number, format, country, date, genre and styles, barcode, production, studio, its photos (front, back, disc, booklet, inside), its credits, its tracks (no., title, duration — the total duration is calculated; 📝 for the lyrics, notes and annotations, the track’s credits and the version) and its editions and pressings (format, label, catalogue number, country, year, barcode). 📋 “Paste a track list” fills everything in at once. Click on a record: its page as on Discogs, with lyrics that unfold.

column2: How do I import a discography from Discogs (or MusicBrainz, Apple Music)?
column3: Catalogue → 💿 Discography → ⤒ Import → Discogs: paste the address of the artist’s page (…discogs.com/artist/…), of an album (…/master/…) or of a record (…/release/…). For an artist, their releases appear to be ticked (appearances unticked); each album comes with its tracks, durations, credits, label, format, covers and the list of its editions. Discogs limits the pace: a little more than one second per record. To search by name, you need a free Discogs token (discogs.com → Settings → Developers) to put in 🔑 Keys. Without a key: MusicBrainz (albums, tracks, editions, covers from the Cover Art Archive), Apple Music (tracks and durations) or Wikidata. The covers are brought into the record’s media (tick box). You need the Internet.

column2: How do I import a filmography (IMDb, TMDb)?
column3: Catalogue → 🎬 Filmography → ⤒ Import: “Wikidata” with the person’s name, or “An IMDb address” (…imdb.com/name/nm…): IMDb has no free access, but Wikidata links each IMDb entry and gives films, jobs (actor, directing, screenplay, music, cinematography, editing, production), roles, director, length and the film’s IMDb identifier. With a free TMDb key (🔑 Keys), “TMDb” adds posters, summaries, cast, countries and companies. Everything can then be corrected by hand (role, awards, festivals, notes).

column2: How do I add a sculpture, a poster, a play, a concerto… (all the types of works)?
column3: In the person’s catalogue: “＋ New work” (on their page) or “＋” at the end of the tabs. The “What kind of work?” window arranges 131 types into 12 families (visual arts, music, stage, writing, moving image and sound, design and crafts, space and landscape, digital and games, model-making and hobbies, tastes and scents, linking records, my types). Type in the box (“bronze”, “opera”, “podcast”, “coppersmith”…), filter by family, then click a type: its record opens with its own fields. “☰ See the list” opens the list of that type instead of a new record. ⚙️ Manage the types: hide those you never use.
